issue.title: [DualToR] orchagent creates a core dump during `config reload` with standby mux ports

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

On an active-standby DualToR system, `orchagent` crashes during `config
reload` when mux ports are in the standby state. The reload command returns
successfully, but a new orchagent core file is created in
`/var/core/`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an active-standby DualToR device with one or more mux ports in the
   `standby` state.
2. Verify the state with `show mux status`.
3. Run `sudo config reload -y`.
4. Run `ls /var/core/` and compare the output with the list before the reload.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual:** `orchagent` creates a core dump during config reload.

**Expected:** config reload completes without orchagent crashing or
creating a new orchagent core file, including when mux ports are in standby.

### Relevant log output

```shell
admin@ldp408:~$ ls /var/core/
orchagent.1785068889.170.core.gz  orchagent.1785069102.255.core.gz

admin@ldp408:~$ sudo config reload -y
Acquired lock on /etc/sonic/reload.lock
...
Restarting SONiC target ...
...
Released lock on /etc/sonic/reload.lock

admin@ldp408:~$ ls /var/core/
orchagent.1785068889.170.core.gz  orchagent.1785069102.255.core.gz  orchagent.1785153078.190.core.gz
```

resolution.title: Fix orchagent  on shutdown in active-standby dualtor topologies.
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it

Fixes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/issues/4829

Fix an `orchagent` SIGSEGV during shutdown/config reload on active-standby
DualToR systems with one or more mux ports in standby. `gAclOrch` is destroyed
before `gMuxOrch` due to `m_orchList` ordering. When MuxAclHandler's destructor
calls `gAclOrch->getAclRule()` on the dangling pointer, it crashes with a null
vtable dereference that creates an orchagent core dump during `config reload`.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it
Rather than reordering m_orchList (which is fragile — PR [#2397](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/pull/2397)
silently broke PR [#2010](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/pull/2010) ordering intent 8 months
later), guard the destructor:

- Clear `gAclOrch` when `AclOrch` is destroyed and skip `MuxAclHandler` ACL
  cleanup when it has already gone away during shutdown.
- Add an explicit `Orch::detachObservers()` shutdown phase before any orch is
  deleted, and implement it for MuxOrch, NeighOrch, and FdbOrch. This removes
  observer/subject destruction-order dependencies.
- Clear the corresponding global pointers in the affected orch destructors.
- Iterate ACL tables by const reference in `AclOrch::getTableById()` to avoid
  copying `AclTable` instances and their `shared_ptr<AclRule>` maps.
- Add a mux integration test that places a mux port in standby, stops
  orchagent, and verifies it stops without a coredump.

#### How to verify it

- On an active-standby DualToR device, put at least one mux port in `standby`,
  run `sudo config reload -y`, and verify that no new `orchagent` core file is
  created in `/var/core/`.
- Run the new `TestMuxShutdownWithStandby` test in `tests/test_mux.py`.
